newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures close limit down on slow cash.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures close limit down on slow cash.

text.p: Continued slow cash trade kept CME lumber futures pressured and sell stops kept prices down as much as the limit of $10.000 per tbf at the close.
Closing limit down were March at $420.00 and May at $380.60 per tbf, with other months closing $9.40 to $2.10 per tbf lower.

Cash trade remained slow in the face of weather related construction problems, and wholesalers apparently were offering wood at a discount. This prompted general liquidation into sell stops, which were hit under $423.50 per tbf, basis March, traders said.

"Wholesalers bought some prouduct last Wednesday and Thursday and the market doesn't seem to be obsorbing it very well so they did some hedge selling early," said Curt Cunningham, President Pacific Futures Trading.

Further losses were expected Wednesday in lumber futures as about 100 sell contracts remained unfilled in March. Options trade also pointed to lower prices with March trading synthetically $8.00 to $9.00 lower, pit sources said.
"We need to stay above $415, $416 (in March) or we are going to start cracking some trend lines," Cunningham added.
